new.name: optical_content_mismatch
new.description: A lens, magnifier, mirror or screen shows content that is not what lies behind/under it (or shows nothing when it should magnify).
examples: orig4/gpt_image_2_quality_high: lens shows a full boot print over plain cobbles; real print is far lower right
orig4/flux3_klein: lens shows his paw, footprint outside it
orig4/qwen_image_2p1_nope: lens empty, instead projects a spotlight circle
new.why_not_v2: A12 mentions reflections only; refraction/magnification and screen content correspondence are not covered.

new.name: convention_coded_marking_error
new.description: Objects whose markings follow a fixed real-world code (pool balls, dice, clock faces, cards, keyboards, traffic lights) show duplicated, invalid or colour-mismatched codes.
examples: phi482/krea2_turbo: '4' on green and on red stripe, '0' on blue
new.why_not_v2: A02/A03 check spelling/legibility, not validity or uniqueness of coded identifiers.

new.name: impossible_device_state
new.description: A functional device is in a state it cannot be in: traffic light with red+green (or all three) lit simultaneously, etc.
examples: phi242/flux3_klein: each head red and green lit
new.why_not_v2: A10 is about physical construction ('could exist and work'), judges rarely apply it to lamp states.

new.name: requested_text_on_wrong_carrier
new.description: Text requested for one place (overlay, sign) bleeds onto another object.
examples: phi242/fibo2_dev: bus destination sign shows '10.4 2023' copied from the timestamp overlay
new.why_not_v2: B04 covers unrequested prompt words, not requested text duplicated onto a wrong surface.

new.name: unrequested_slogan_text
new.description: Model inserts invented slogans/titles/brand copy on posters, books, mugs, billboards ('A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'TRUTH ALWAYS FINDS ITS WAY'). Spelled correctly, so passes A02/A03, but changes the image's message.
new.why_not_v2: B07 requires scene-changing extras; B04 only prompt words. Systematic in sunburst models across 5/10 prompts.

new.name: viewer_facing_document_orientation
new.description: A page being drawn/written/read by an in-scene person is oriented for the camera, i.e. upside-down for that person.
examples: orig123/flux3_klein: signature reads upright from camera while Leonardo draws from the far side
orig123/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: Vitruvian figure on parchment upright to viewer
new.why_not_v2: No criterion addresses orientation consistency between an object and its in-scene user.

new.name: unintended_translucency
new.description: A solid object becomes partly see-through where it overlaps another layer (double exposure), without being glass or ghost.
examples: orig365/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: ring stones visible through Jupiter's lower limb
new.why_not_v2: A11 covers ordering, A15 pasted-in elements; neither names see-through solids.

new.name: internal_text_inconsistency
new.description: Two legible, correctly spelled strings contradict each other (name in header vs caption, mismatched IDs).
examples: orig483/gemini_3_1_flash_image: header 'Pet Lana' with caption 'Luna's new toy!'
phi1/gpt_image_2: well-formed but invalid orientation codes 'AHL','PHA','RHA'
new.why_not_v2: A02 measures letter accuracy only.

new.name: slogan_filler_text
new.description: Unrequested, correctly-spelled motivational/marketing slogans stamped on many surfaces (posters, erasers, laptops, concrete, pods). Template set-dressing made of text.
examples: phi378/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: slogans on 8 surfaces incl. eraser 'Keep Going', robot 'Better Learners Brighter Tomorrows'
phi134/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: 'BUILD SAFER SMARTER TOGETHER' on banner, 'PROGRESS BUILDS TOMORROW' on concrete
orig375/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'LIFE PRESERVATION FOR A BRIGHTER TOMORROW' etched on cryo-pod
new.why_not_v2: A02/A03 only fire on misspellings; B04 covers prompt words leaking; B07 lists objects (brick walls, plants) not text. Correct but unrequested text has no home.

new.name: semantic_text_error
new.description: Text spelled correctly but factually/semantically impossible: wrong station names, impossible dates, wrong place combos.
new.why_not_v2: A02 checks letters, not meaning; no rule on well-formed-but-wrong text.

new.name: wrong_tool_form / functional object misrender
new.description: A specific functional instrument replaced by a lookalike that cannot do the job (laryngoscope -> pen/rod/dental probe/syringe, LiDAR -> camera, hose plugged into laryngoscope).
examples: phi10/flux3_klein_base: long curved probe instead of laryngoscope
phi10/krea2_turbo: breathing hose attached to laryngoscope handle
new.why_not_v2: Split between A10 and B02 with no guidance for 'nearly the right tool'; judges disagree on which code.

new.name: temporal_moment_mismatch
new.description: Prompt specifies a moment (before impact, mid-swing) and the image shows a different moment (impact under way, debris burst).
examples: phi495/ideogram4_nf4: ball hitting wall with debris
new.why_not_v2: B03 is about action/pose; 'timing of an event' is not mentioned, so judges skip it.

new.name: prompt_word_literalism
new.description: A figurative word is rendered literally (cactus 'branch' as arm -> real woody tree branch with leaves).
examples: orig495/qwen_image_2p1_pe: cactus arm becomes leafy tree branch
new.why_not_v2: Shows up as A08 fusion but the cause is semantic; a B-level check 'figurative language rendered literally' would catch it more reliably.

new.name: viewpoint_device_in_frame
new.description: Prompt describes the capturing device/POV (surveillance camera mounted high, dashcam, drone) and the model draws that device inside the image, often large and occluding the scene.
examples: phi262/qwen_image_2p1_nope: giant dome camera hangs in centre occluding forklift load
phi262/gemini, gpt_image_2_quality_high, ideogram4_nf4: smaller dome in corner
new.why_not_v2: B07 lists extras that change the scene but not the specific failure of rendering the camera instead of shooting from it; B08 is about shot size.

new.name: simile_literalisation
new.description: A comparison in the prompt ('flying like a flock of birds', 'resembles a lightsaber') is rendered as the compared entity itself or fused into the subject.
examples: orig508/ideogram4_nf4: real robins among the flying books
orig508/qwen_image_2p1_nope: every flying book has a bird head and body attached
new.why_not_v2: B02 checks requested objects present, not that compared-to entities must be absent; A08 catches only the fused variant.

new.name: unrequested_slogan_text
new.description: Model inserts clean, well-spelled motivational slogans/captions on banners, posters and plaques that were not requested.
new.why_not_v2: A02/A03 only flag misspellings; B04 only flags prompt words leaking into text. A recurring model-signature slogan passes everything.

new.name: hybrid_as_juxtaposition
new.description: 'X has grown Y' / 'X made of Y' rendered as a separate Y placed on/next to X (butterfly perched on teapot; jellyfish decorating a steel tower) rather than a true hybrid.
examples: orig23/krea2_turbo: butterfly perched on handle of a teapot sitting on a rock
orig23/flux3_klein: teapot stacked on a full butterfly body
orig145/fibo2_dev: steel tower with jellyfish ornaments
new.why_not_v2: B02 sees both objects present and passes; B05 material check is not phrased for composition-type hybrids.

new.name: load_support_mismatch
new.description: A lifting/carrying machine's load is not on its lifting element (forks on floor while load hangs at mast top; forks raised empty while pallet sits on rack).
examples: phi262/qwen_image_2p1_nope: forks on floor, pallets stuck to mast top
phi262/flux3_klein_base: forks down, pallet above mast
new.why_not_v2: Fits A09/A10 loosely; VLMs miss it because each object looks fine; worth an explicit example under A09 (mechanical support).

new.name: functional_semantics_inconsistency (traffic/diagram logic)
new.description: Signs, road markings, arrows or diagram annotations are each well formed, but their combined meaning is contradictory or nonsensical: opposing flow arrows, double-headed lane arrows, meshing gears drawn rotating the same way, a yield line drawn as a zebra.
examples: phi399/flux3_klein: near-side circulatory arrows point left while the chevrons point right
phi399/flux3_klein_base: up/down double arrow in the ego lane
orig155/gemini_3_1_flash_image: both meshing gears annotated clockwise
phi399/fibo2_dev: left arrow and right-curving arrow in one entry lane
new.why_not_v2: A10 asks whether a diagram makes sense, but VLMs read it as object structure; A19 covers out-of-place objects, not wrong semantics among in-place ones.

new.name: container_continuity_violation
new.description: The contents of a transparent container are larger than the container where they sit, the glass wall vanishes or ends at the content, or content appears outside the walls.
examples: orig399/gpt_image_2: Earth 2x the width of the hourglass neck, glass walls vanish into it
orig399/flux3_klein: sand rings orbit outside the glass
orig399/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: glass ends at the globe
new.why_not_v2: A08 covers interpenetration of opaque objects; transparent glass makes the violation subtle, and none of the examples cover containers.

new.name: material_state_error
new.description: A material is shown in the wrong physical state, such as solid agar as liquid broth with floating beads, or colonies visible inside the gel depth.
examples: phi34/krea2_turbo: deep liquid agar with floating bead colonies, colonies seen through the side wall
phi34/gpt_image_2: colonies look like droplets on liquid
new.why_not_v2: A12 lists liquids and cloth behaviour but not the case where a solid is rendered as a liquid.

new.name: competing_unrequested_text
new.description: Correctly spelled, legible but unrequested slogans or labels added near or behind the requested text, diluting it or paraphrasing the prompt.
examples: orig514/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 5 sharp background slogans around the requested T-shirt quote
new.why_not_v2: B04 covers prompt words as unrequested text only partly; B07 is about objects. A03 does not apply because the text is not pseudo-text.

new.name: requested_format_missing
new.description: The prompt names an output format or genre (an app onboarding page, a poster, a UI), and the model renders only the subject illustration with no format elements.
examples: orig38: 7 of 12 models (fibo2_dev, flux3_klein, gpt_image_2, gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high, ideogram4_nf4, krea2_turbo, qwen_image_2p1_nope) have no UI chrome
new.why_not_v2: B05 covers style and medium; it is ambiguous whether a missing page or UI wrapper is B02 or B05.

new.name: slogan_stuffing
new.description: Unrequested invented corporate/motivational slogans scattered on walls, boxes, clothing and monitors to make a scene look 'designed'.
examples: phi287/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: six slogans incl. 'LOGISTICS FOR A BRIGHTER TOMORROW' on a worker's shirt
phi287/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'SAME DAY A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'PACK SHIP REPEAT'
new.why_not_v2: B07 lists template set dressing (brick walls, plants, bystanders) but not text; A03 only checks legibility, and these slogans are perfectly spelled.

new.name: ego_viewpoint_misplacement
new.description: The implied camera/vehicle sits in a physically or legally wrong place (dashcam straddling the double-yellow centreline).
new.why_not_v2: All criteria judge visible objects; nothing covers where the viewer/camera itself is. Closest is A19.

new.name: flow_from_empty_source
new.description: A stream (sand, liquid, molten metal) flows out of a container that is visibly empty.
examples: orig45/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: sand thread from an empty upper bulb
phi528/flux3_klein: molten stream from a dark empty crucible
new.why_not_v2: Fits A12 but no example; VLMs rarely check source-sink consistency.

new.name: unanchored_wing/appendage
new.description: Fantasy appendages (wings) float beside a figure with no attachment point to the body.
examples: orig169/ideogram4_nf4: one wing hangs beside her shoulder while she faces camera
new.why_not_v2: A05 is about limbs; wings/tails on fantasy characters not mentioned, A09 is about objects.

new.name: slogan_injection
new.description: Unrequested feel-good marketing copy (posters, banners, engraved rocks, tab labels) such as 'A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'For a Kinder World', 'CLEAN WORKSPACE SAFE SCIENCE' inserted into scenes. Text is spelled correctly, so A02/A03 never fire; it is a model-signature behaviour.
examples: orig53/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: rocks engraved 'A Happier Playlist Ahead', 'Pets Make Life Sound Better'
orig174/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: banners 'A BRIGHTER HUMAN TOMORROW', 'BEAUTY CONNECTS US'
new.why_not_v2: B04 covers prompt words leaking into the image; B07 needs extras that change the scene. Correctly spelled, unrequested text that adds a message is not named anywhere. Suggest a B04 sub-clause: 'unrequested legible slogans/taglines' (minor; moderate when prominent).

new.name: functional_graphic_state_mismatch
new.description: A functional UI/graphic element contradicts itself: progress indicator not where the fill ends, two controls for one function, time shown three times, template field labels ('Title', 'Artist', 'Time') shown as content.
examples: orig53/qwen_image_2p1_pe: dark fill to mid-bar, caterpillar at the start; hedgehog 'Paused' plus a second pause button
orig53/krea2_turbo: slider thumb and caterpillar both mark progress
new.why_not_v2: A18 checks alignment, overlaps and hierarchy, not semantics. A07 'duplicated UI card' partly fits. v3 A18 should add: 'state consistency — indicator, fill and labels agree; one control per function; no placeholder captions'.

new.name: attribute_binding_to_wrong_entity
new.description: A requested attribute appears on the image but on the wrong object (the colour of the elapsed path is painted on the caterpillar).
examples: orig53/fibo2_dev: caterpillar's rear segments dark green, branch stays brown
new.why_not_v2: B05 asks whether the attribute is realised, so a judge sees 'dark green present' and passes it. Needs explicit 'bound to the right object' wording (the Layer B preamble mentions it but B05 does not).

new.name: hose/cable_topology_error
new.description: Linear flexible objects (hoses, cables, ropes) whose ends do not make sense: both ends run into the same reel, the held object is mid-span with a coupling, a hose dives into a puddle like a solid surface.
examples: phi294/flux3_klein: both hose ends go into the reel, gripper holds a mid-span coupling
phi294/krea2_turbo: gripper clamps the reel hub
phi294/qwen_image_2p1_nope: hose pierces a puddle with a splash
new.why_not_v2: A10 is about manufactured objects working; A12 about cloth/liquid. Tracing a continuous object end-to-end is not prompted. Add to A10: 'trace hoses, cables, ropes, chains end to end'.

new.name: inverted_relief / negative-space error
new.description: An impression, mould, dent or engraving is rendered as a raised positive shape (or vice versa): a hand imprint that bulges up as a fabric hand, a footprint that is a raised foot.
examples: phi545/fibo2_dev: hand print is a convex fabric hand with palm creases sitting in a pit
new.why_not_v2: A12 talks about rigid shape and gravity; nothing asks whether a trace is concave or convex. VLMs see "a hand shape" and pass it.

new.name: trace_cause_mismatch
new.description: A trace does not match the thing that made it: wiped area not under the wiper, imprint with wrong digit count or mirrored copies, shadows starting in mid-air instead of at the object, rain drops on a dashboard indoors.
examples: phi420/ideogram4_nf4: clean dome-shaped area sits below wipers that rest in the upper glass
phi545/flux3_klein_base: one palm with 5 finger grooves up and 5 down
orig189/gemini_3_1_flash_image: three shadows fan out from one point in the sand
phi420/flux3_klein: rain drops beaded on the interior dashboard
new.why_not_v2: A12 says "cause produces effect" but only with examples of missing effects (no wet ground); it does not ask whether a present effect matches its cause in location, count and geometry.

new.name: required_text_occluded
new.description: A requested text string is partly hidden behind a foreground subject, so letters are missing although rendered correctly.
examples: orig540/gpt_image_2: shoulder covers "t" of through and "e" of expectation
orig540/gpt_image_2_quality_high: woman's head covers "e" of expectation
new.why_not_v2: A02 checks glyphs, A17 only frame edges, B04 equality of legible text; occlusion falls between them.

new.name: inconsistent_implied_altitude
new.description: Aerial or satellite views mix cues from different heights: planetary horizon curvature with block-level detail, or fisheye tilt without a lens reason.
examples: phi68/flux3_klein_base: orbital curvature with ships readable as from ~2 km
new.why_not_v2: A11 covers convergence and order, A20 relative sizes; neither covers camera-height consistency.

new.name: layer_order_paradox
new.description: In flat 2D art an element is drawn in front of a second element at one point and behind it at another without any wrap-around, so the drawing is self-contradictory (or an object enters and exits a body with no visible path).
examples: orig75/flux3_klein: bamboo in front of the panda's forehead, yet nose and mouth drawn over the bamboo
orig75/flux3_klein_base: bamboo pokes out above the head between the ears and reappears below the mouth
new.why_not_v2: A08 describes interpenetration in 3D and A11 is gated on 'scene has depth'; flat vector images are easy to exempt from both. Add explicit wording: occlusion order must be consistent even in flat styles.

new.name: copyrighted_character_lookalike
new.description: Generated figure reproduces a recognisable fictional character (costume, hair accessory, companion animal) typically triggered by an artist/studio style cue.
examples: orig195/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: girl with red bow and dark dress = Kiki
orig195/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: red-bow girl with black cat = Kiki and Jiji
new.why_not_v2: C01 covers real trademarks, real persons and real landmarks only.

new.name: filter_layer_effect
new.description: A requested physical effect (rain-washed ink, blur) is applied as a uniform 2D filter over a whole element, ignoring the surface it sits on, so the element looks like a separate blurred layer.
examples: orig554/krea2_turbo: entire text block Gaussian-blurred while paper creases are sharp and the letters ignore the wrinkles
new.why_not_v2: Partly A15 (decal ignoring surface) and partly B05, but neither says 'effect applied uniformly as a filter instead of locally/physically'.

new.name: style_triggered_protagonist
new.description: A style or studio reference ('Miyazaki style') causes the model to add a stock protagonist who becomes the focal subject of a scene-only prompt.
examples: orig195/gpt_image_2: girl with book fills left third
orig195/gpt_image_2_quality_high: girl and cat at desk
new.why_not_v2: B07 covers it in principle, but its examples (bystander, brick walls) do not cue VLMs to flag a large, attractive added main character.

new.name: emission_source_mismatch
new.description: A flow or emission the prompt ties to a specific part (rain from a spout, smoke from a chimney, light from a lamp) comes from the wrong part of the object, or from several parts, while the intended outlet is inert.
examples: orig448/qwen_image_2p1_pe: a water torrent pours from a hole in the bottom of the pot, spout dry
orig448/fibo2_dev: rain drips from the base of the pot
orig448/flux3_klein_base, qwen_image_2p1_nope: rain curtain falls from the whole underside, not the spout
new.why_not_v2: A12 cause/effect covers 'fire gives light' but not 'the effect comes from the right outlet'; B03 is the only fallback and gives no Layer-A signal when there is no prompt.

new.name: embedded_data_inconsistency (maps/charts/screens)
new.description: Information rendered inside a map, chart or UI contradicts itself or plain geography: legend range vs labels, scale bar vs the land shown, identical values repeated across different terrain, feature labels in the wrong place, a route crossing land, duplicated map furniture.
examples: phi80/gpt_image_2: legend -4100…-6200 m but labels read -6800 m
phi80/qwen_image_2p1_pe: 1:250,000 / 25 nm scale with all of Cuba on screen
phi80/fibo2_dev: cable runs over land; deep-water labels on the shallow shelf
phi80/krea2_turbo: two north arrows, '20m' ocean depths
new.why_not_v2: A10 says only 'does every diagram make sense', with circuit/UI examples. Judges don't know whether world-knowledge or geographic errors count, or how to grade them; A18 covers only alignment and layout.

new.name: functional_part_misplacement
new.description: A tool or vessel has its functional parts in a non-working arrangement, e.g. handle and spout on the same side, or a vessel with an extra opening.
examples: orig448/flux3_klein: teapot handle arcs directly above the spout on the same side
orig323/qwen_image_2p1_pe: one-sided ring flap on a mushroom stalk
new.why_not_v2: It falls under A10, but A10's examples are all machines and UI. Adding 'part arrangement on everyday objects (handles, spouts, lids)' would make judges look for it.

new.name: tool_output_mismatch
new.description: The effect produced by an instrument does not match the instrument's contents or state (white-cream piping bag writes brown chocolate lines; pen colour vs ink).
examples: orig574/qwen_image_2p1_nope: white cream bag, all letters brown chocolate
new.why_not_v2: A12 cause->effect examples are environmental physics; a VLM does not check tool contents vs produced marks.

new.name: anthropomorphic_end_effector
new.description: Human body parts (gloved hand, fingers) grafted onto machines/robots, or robots using human hand tools as if they were people.
examples: phi93/flux3_klein_base: black gloved hand at ABB wrist holds gravity spray gun
phi93/krea2_turbo: grey gloved hand at robot wrist grips pistol gun
new.why_not_v2: A05 is about bodies, A10 about machines working; the hybrid human-machine part is in neither's examples.

new.name: screen_viewpoint_logic
new.description: Content shown on a screen/feed/mirror contradicts its stated source (an excavator's forward camera showing the whole excavator in third person).
examples: phi338/fibo2_dev, flux3_klein, flux3_klein_base, ideogram4_nf4, krea2_turbo, qwen x2: monitor shows whole excavator from outside
new.why_not_v2: B03/B06 check interactions and placement, not logical consistency of depicted media.

new.name: invented_slogan_flooding
new.description: Generator fills posters, mugs, hats, vests, notebooks with unrequested motivational/brand slogans, turning set dressing into text-heavy template.
examples: phi338/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'REAL SITES REAL PROGRESS', 'SAFER CLEANER STRONGER', 'BUILD SMARTER TOGETHER', 'PLAN OPERATE IMPROVE'
new.why_not_v2: B04 only flags prompt words written as text; B07 lists brick walls/plants as template dressing but not invented slogans; A03 only checks if text is gibberish, and these are correctly spelled.

new.name: semantic_text_error
new.description: Legible, correctly spelled technical text that is nonsensical in context (non-existent package codes, mismatched part specs).
new.why_not_v2: A02/A03 are letter-level only.

new.name: decal_orientation_mismatch
new.description: Printed text/logo stays upright to the viewer although the object it is printed on is tipped or rotated.
examples: orig339/qwen_image_2p1_pe: toppled mug with horizontally upright Japanese text
new.why_not_v2: A15 mentions decals ignoring curvature only, not object pose.

new.name: mixed_altitude_viewpoint
new.description: Foreground shot from ground level combined with a background seen from orbit/altitude (planet limb behind beach surf).
examples: orig458/krea2_turbo: beach waves running up to curved Earth limb
new.why_not_v2: A11 is phrased as line convergence/overlap ordering.

new.name: process_state_inconsistency
new.description: An object shows the result of a process at a stage before that process happens (printed traces on the unwind/supply reel, sealant on parts not yet dispensed).
examples: phi221/gpt_image_2: supply reel already covered in circuit traces
phi221/flux3_klein: both reels and drum printed
phi221/gpt_image_2_quality_high: film leaving unwind reel already printed
new.why_not_v2: A10 covers objects that could not work, A12 physics; neither covers cause-order of a depicted workflow. Proposed: extend A12 'cause produces effect' with 'effects must appear only downstream of their cause'.

new.name: unrequested_slogan_and_branding_text
new.description: Model fills walls, glass and machines with marketing slogans and real brand logos ('A CLEANER TOMORROW', 'HUMAN IN THE LOOP FOR A SAFER TOMORROW', KUKA, Henkel, TOYOTA, COGNEX).
examples: phi340/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'HUMAN IN THE LOOP FOR A SAFER TOMORROW', TOYOTA
phi101/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'SCA Bonding for a cleaner tomorrow', Henkel
new.why_not_v2: B07 lists template set dressing objects but not text; A03 only fires on pseudo-text, and these slogans are spelled correctly. A systematic stylistic tic of one model family goes unflagged.

new.name: unrequested_thematic_text_overlay
new.description: Equations / captions floating in the scene because they are stereotypically associated with the subject (Einstein -> E=mc²).
examples: orig469/qwen_image_2p1_pe: column of chalk equations and a graph
new.why_not_v2: B04 only covers prompt words rendered as text; associated-concept text is not covered.

new.name: material_weathering_leak
new.description: Weathering specific to one material (bronze verdigris) spread onto an adjacent different material (granite base).
examples: orig583/flux3_klein: green patina blotches on gray stone base
new.why_not_v2: Fits A22 in spirit but A22 examples are uniform grime/grain; add explicit 'material-specific wear on the wrong material' example.

new.name: unrequested_slogan_text
new.description: Well-spelled motivational or thematic slogans that nobody asked for, used as set dressing on billboards, banners and bins ('A BRIGHTER TOMORROW', 'HUMANITY PERSISTS'). Often the same phrase repeats across several signs in one image.
examples: phi112/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst_quality_high: 'PLASTICS SHAPE A BRIGHTER TOMORROW' + 'BETTER PARTS A STRONGER TOMORROW'
new.why_not_v2: A03 catches only pseudo-text. B04 covers only quoted prompt text and prompt-word leakage. B07 covers only extras that change the scene. Well-formed but editorialising text falls between all three. It is a strong fingerprint of one model family (5/9 prompts).

new.name: wrong_symbol_or_icon
new.description: A pictogram, icon or standard symbol is wrong for the object it sits on, even when the text is spelled correctly. Examples are a road-sign glyph whose meaning contradicts the sign text, or a nonsense icon.
examples: phi477/gpt_image_2: two-way-traffic arrows on a DIVIDED HIGHWAY BEGINS sign
new.why_not_v2: A02/A03 judge letters only. B02 is about objects. Icons and standard symbols have no home, so judges pass these signs as 'text correct'.

new.name: technical_term_literalism
new.description: A technical or compound term is drawn by its literal words instead of what it means in the domain.
examples: phi239/flux3_klein_base: 'cable chains' drawn as drooping metal link chains
phi239/krea2_turbo: concrete 'beads' as rows of balls, with pellets spilled at the base
phi353/qwen_image_2p1_nope: 'brain-computer interface' headset drawn as a brain-textured cap
new.why_not_v2: B02 says 'right kind, including real-world object', but judges treat the literal object as matching the noun. An explicit rule that domain terms are judged by their domain meaning is needed.

new.name: functional_logic_violation
new.description: A scene breaks the operating rules of the domain. Examples are a vehicle in the opposing lanes driving away from the camera (wrong-way), a person inside a robot cell with no guard, or a robot outside its own enclosure.
examples: phi477/flux3_klein_base: pickup on the opposing side of the new median, seen from behind
phi353/krea2_turbo: operator handles the bracket the robot is gripping, no screen
phi353/qwen_image_2p1_pe: robot outside the glass enclosure
new.why_not_v2: A19 covers out-of-place objects and A12 physics. Rule or affordance violations (traffic direction, safety guarding) are not named, so judges miss them.

issues.problem: Wheel/leg counts on vehicles need counting per visible side and inferring the hidden side; judges miscount. Rule needs guidance for symmetric objects.
issues.proposed_fix: Add: for bilaterally symmetric objects count one visible side and double; flag when visible side alone contradicts the count.

issues.problem: Featureless faces in low-poly/mannequin styles: unclear whether stylistic.
issues.proposed_fix: Count as minor A06 unless the style family normally omits faces (mannequin, chess piece) and the prompt implies no expression.

issues.problem: Cause/effect timing in frozen action not explicit; effect shown before cause.
examples: phi482/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: cue ball still at cue tip while rack explodes
issues.proposed_fix: Add example: struck/acting object still at rest while its effect has already happened.

issues.problem: Requested overlays (timestamps/HUD) are fine, but medium-native borders (watercolour paper margin) are ambiguous.
issues.proposed_fix: Border native to the requested medium is not A16 unless it consumes >10% of the canvas or crops focal content.

issues.problem: 'Examining X with a tool' needs the tool aimed at X; many models hold the magnifier in the air.
issues.proposed_fix: Add: instrument-use actions require the instrument's working end to point at the named target.

issues.problem: Concept-art prompts legitimately yield character sheets with inset panels; A16 says 'split panel' is a defect.
issues.proposed_fix: Split panels/insets are intended when the requested medium is concept art, character sheet, storyboard, comic, or reference sheet.

issues.problem: 'To her left ... to her right' with a camera-facing subject: all 12 models used viewer-left; strictly that is mirrored. Rubric does not say which frame to use.
examples: orig375: all 12 models put pod at viewer-left
issues.proposed_fix: When left/right is relative to a character facing the camera, accept either frame (or explicitly default to viewer frame) and do not flag; only flag when both objects are on the same side.

issues.problem: Requested timecode/overlay text (CCTV) has no quoted string; is it A02 or B04? Malformed timecode should be A02 major since it is the requested text.
issues.proposed_fix: Requested-but-unquoted text (timecode, date, label) is A02 intended text; judge its format plausibility (valid date/time) rather than exact string.

issues.problem: CCTV prompts ask for compression artifacts and motion blur; nearly every model outputs a clean photo. B05 mentions grain/blur but not compression/CCTV looks, and A21-A23 might penalise them if present.
issues.proposed_fix: List compression artifacts, low-res CCTV, scanlines in B05 looks; state that requested degradation is excluded from A21/A23.

issues.problem: Notebooks full of pseudo-math are everywhere; unclear whether a notebook a prompt mentions ('math notes') is intended text (A02) or incidental (A03).
issues.proposed_fix: Text whose content the prompt names (math notes, a menu) is A02; grade it as content-correct vs pseudo-glyph.

issues.problem: Lists 'signature, seal' as overlay, but seals and inscriptions are native to requested Chinese ink painting; strict reading over-flags 9/12 orig23 images.
examples: orig23/qwen_image_2p1_pe: real inscription 澄心遠趣 with seals
orig23/gemini: 云山飞壶 with seals
issues.proposed_fix: Exempt medium-idiomatic marks (seals, colophons, artist signatures in traditional painting) from A16; judge their glyphs under A03 instead.

issues.problem: Unclear whether unrequested decorative calligraphy is 'incidental' (A03) or 'intended' (A02); gibberish calligraphy is common.
examples: orig23/gpt_image_2: three columns of invented glyphs
issues.proposed_fix: State: unrequested inscriptions/colophons are incidental -> A03; severity moderate when they are large and prominent in the composition.

issues.problem: Focal object rendered photographically on a painted background is the most common failure in the ink-wash prompt, but rubric example is 'colour tiger in charcoal room'; VLMs tend to accept it because the object looks high quality.
issues.proposed_fix: Add example: 'photoreal product-shot object pasted into a requested ink/watercolour painting = A15 moderate, on focal'.

issues.problem: In fantasy scenes floating items may be intended magic; rubric gives no rule.
issues.proposed_fix: In non-photographic/fantasy mode, flag floating only if the prompt states attachment or the scene's own logic shows support elsewhere; otherwise treat as style intent.

issues.problem: Examples are all parts (heads, poles); a duplicated unique entity (landmark) isn't mentioned.
examples: orig145/qwen_image_2p1_pe: second normal Eiffel Tower beside the jellyfish one
issues.proposed_fix: Add: 'a unique named entity (landmark, specific person) appearing twice' is A07.

issues.problem: Rubric checks spelling but not semantic validity of formatted data (dates, times). '2023-14' has no misspelt glyph.
issues.proposed_fix: Under A02: formatted strings (dates, times, prices, phone numbers) must be valid in their format; an impossible month/garbled field counts as an error.

issues.problem: Directional relations like 'hugs from behind' are failed by 8/12 models with symmetric side-by-side hugs; judges tend to accept any hug.
issues.proposed_fix: Add explicit instruction: verify the direction/role of each interaction (who is behind/in front, who acts on whom); a symmetric version of an asymmetric action is a B03 moderate.

issues.problem: No explicit guidance for mechanisms (gears) or functional markings, so overlapping coplanar gears and contradictory arrows are easy to pass.
examples: orig155/krea2_turbo red gear superimposed on blue
orig155: 7/12 gears overlap rather than mesh
issues.proposed_fix: Add: "For mechanisms, gears must interleave without overlapping, meshing gears counter-rotate, and belts and chains must close. Arrows and markings must not contradict each other."

issues.problem: Prompts with negated physics ("sand does NOT flow down") or partial reveals ("only ears and eyes visible") fail most often; v2 has no note that the stereotypical default (sand falls, whole fox shown) is the failure mode to check.
examples: orig276: 6/12 show the full fox face or body
issues.proposed_fix: Add to Layer B: "When the prompt negates a default behaviour or limits visibility, verify that the default did not occur; the default is major when it is the prompt's point."

issues.problem: A font or style switch inside one word (italic "on" in "rebellion") is not listed.
issues.proposed_fix: Add "inconsistent typeface/weight/slant within one string" to the A02 checklist.

issues.problem: Quote marks from the prompt printed into the image, and prompt jargon ("ego") leaking into overlays, are unaddressed.
issues.proposed_fix: Printed prompt delimiters = minor B04; prompt meta-words (ego, photorealistic, 35mm) written into the image = B04 moderate.

issues.problem: It does not separate requested brands from injected ones.
examples: phi150/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst "United Rentals" truck when only Boston Dynamics was requested
issues.proposed_fix: Report requested vs unrequested brands separately.

issues.problem: Requested camera height or angle ("upward from street level", "low dashcam") has no clear home: B08 is shot size and B06 is layout.
examples: phi511/fibo2_dev looks down on the roof
issues.proposed_fix: Extend B08 to "shot size, framing and camera viewpoint/height/angle".

issues.problem: Prompts that specify states or negations ('upper bulb empty', 'containing no sand at all', 'not flapping') have no clear code; I used B05 but it's neither attribute nor action.
examples: orig45/krea2_turbo: sand in both bulbs of the hourglass that must be empty
orig45/qwen_image_2p1_pe: sand at bottom of the 'no sand' hourglass
issues.proposed_fix: Add B09 state_negation: object state, fill level, on/off, explicit 'no X' about a requested object. Severity major when the negation is the point of the prompt.

issues.problem: Character-share scoring does not penalise correct words in wrong order or a sentence split across pages out of sequence.
examples: orig524/flux3_klein: 'Knowledge always / to a brighter future.' + 'illuminates the path to'
orig524/qwen_image_2p1_pe: 'the path to' duplicated across lines
issues.proposed_fix: State that word-order errors and repeated phrases each count as wrong words; text must read correctly in natural reading order.

issues.problem: Left/right of character vs viewer is not defined; many models point with the wrong hand.
examples: orig524/flux3_klein and flux3_klein_base point with the character's left hand
issues.proposed_fix: Add: 'left/right in a prompt refers to the character's own side unless the prompt says viewer's'; wrong hand = moderate.

issues.problem: Small sparkle logo marks in starry/fantasy scenes are easily read as scene sparkles.
examples: orig169/ideogram4_nf4: grey 4-point sparkle in bottom-right corner
issues.proposed_fix: Add: a flat, unlit glyph in a corner that ignores scene lighting/perspective is a watermark.

issues.problem: Focal illustration cut by its own container inside a UI is neither frame crop nor obviously A18.
examples: orig400/flux3_klein_base: Notre Dame drawing cut off at portal level inside the glass card
issues.proposed_fix: A18: 'an element clipped by its container or overlapped by another UI element'.

issues.problem: Rack/rows with overlapping rims make counts hard; doubled rims (fibo) are A07 vs extra tubes (qwen nope) B01.
issues.proposed_fix: Add example: a second rim/ghost outline on the same item is A07; a complete extra item is B01 (already in boundary rule, add a glassware example).

issues.problem: Left/right relative to a character facing the camera is ambiguous: 10 of 12 models placed 'to his left' on the viewer's left.
examples: orig414: crater viewer-left/prints viewer-right in fibo2_dev, flux3_klein, gpt_image_2, qwen models
issues.proposed_fix: State that 'his/her left' means the subject's own frame; when the subject faces the viewer this is the viewer's right. Either score a mirror swap as minor B06 or declare it tolerated, but define it.

issues.problem: Light direction vs. shadow direction is the most common photographic failure here, but A12 does not give a concrete check, and judges let 'shadow toward the light' and 'front-lit subject with a backlit shadow' pass.
examples: orig414/gemini: sun top-left, shadow goes left
orig414/flux3_klein: shadow toward camera, suit evenly front-lit
orig294/gpt_image_2p5_sunburst: one robe, two diverging shadows
issues.proposed_fix: Add explicit sub-checks: (1) shadows point away from the visible/implied light; (2) the lit side of the subject matches the shadow direction; (3) one occluder casts one connected shadow of matching shape; (4) a transparent object casts a light, caustic shadow, not a solid black one.

issues.problem: Requested text rendered tiny and illegible could be excused by the codec-limit rule.
examples: orig535/ideogram4_nf4: the warning line is a green scribble on a small screen
issues.proposed_fix: Rule 3 should state it never applies to text the prompt requests; illegible requested text is A02 (major if it is the requested headline) and B04.

issues.problem: Requested text repeated on a second unrequested surface (head screen + chest screen) and word-level duplication across a line break are not clearly assigned.
examples: orig535/qwen_image_2p1_nope: same warning on head and chest screens with different errors
issues.proposed_fix: Clarify: repeated word inside the string = A02; the whole requested string duplicated on an extra surface = A07 (+B04 if the copies differ).

issues.problem: In UI mock-ups models paste photographic assets (photo hedgehog) into flat/cartoon UI. Album-art photos are legitimately photographic, so judges need a rule for which elements may be photographic.
examples: orig53/qwen_image_2p1_nope: photo hedgehog button next to clay caterpillar and flat icons
issues.proposed_fix: In UI/graphic mode, content panes (album art, thumbnails) may be any style; controls and icons should share one style. A photographic control in an illustrated UI is A15.

issues.problem: "Cause produces effect" lists missing effects only; judges do not check that a present effect matches its cause in position, count, direction, or the side of a barrier it is on.
examples: phi420/fibo2_dev rain on the interior dashboard
issues.proposed_fix: Add sub-check: "Every trace (shadow, imprint, wiped area, splash, wake) starts at its cause, has the cause's shape and count, and lies on the physically reachable side of glass/roofs. Sun shadows are parallel."

issues.problem: The prompt says "animation scene" but 6 of 12 models made photoreal composites. v2 says the requested style decides the mode, but gives no rule on whether a photoreal output of an animation request is judged photographic (and B05 flagged) or non_photographic.
issues.proposed_fix: State: mode for Layer A follows what is rendered; a mismatch with the requested medium is recorded once under B05 (moderate when the whole image is in the wrong medium).

issues.problem: Solid figures merging into fluids (a statue whose robe becomes a water spout) can be a defect or a deliberate VFX look.
issues.proposed_fix: Count it as A08 unless the prompt asks for a transformation or dissolve; cap at moderate when the effect is clearly stylised.

issues.criterion: B01 vs B02 for symbol variants
issues.problem: A requested symbol rendered as a related symbol (eighth note -> beamed pair or sixteenths) does not fit "count" or "object kind" cleanly.
issues.proposed_fix: Wrong symbol variant = B02; a malformed glyph that is no valid symbol = A10.

issues.problem: Dashcam timestamps, film borders and paper edges come with the requested genre ("dashcam footage", "retro film"), but the A16 wording would flag them.
issues.proposed_fix: Exclude overlays implied by the requested medium from A16; still check their text under A02.

issues.problem: Explicit relative-size comparisons between entities ('bamboo thicker than its body', 'immense size vs gentle action') have no clear code. A20 says size words are Layer B context but no B code owns them.
examples: orig75: all 12 models draw bamboo thinner than the body
issues.proposed_fix: Add 'stated sizes and size comparisons' to B05 (attribute) or a dedicated B09 size_comparison; severity moderate when the comparison is an explicit testpoint.

issues.problem: 'To its left' (subject-relative) vs viewer-left ambiguity. All 12 bears have the sapling on viewer's left = the bear's right.
issues.proposed_fix: State a default: when the subject faces the viewer and the prompt says 'to its left', accept either reading unless the prompt says 'from the viewer's perspective'; do not flag.

issues.problem: Prompt quotes text with trailing sentence punctuation inside the quotes ('...dreams,'). Some models copy the comma, others drop it or add a period. Unclear which is correct.
issues.proposed_fix: Ignore trailing punctuation that belongs to the prompt sentence; at most minor B04, never A02.

issues.problem: When the prompt requests degraded text (rain-washed, blurred letters), smeared letters are correct; letter-by-letter reading would penalise them.
issues.proposed_fix: If degradation is requested, count a character as correct when its identity is still inferable or its smearing is consistent with the requested effect; flag only substituted/invented letters.

issues.problem: Requests like 'low sun from the northwest' need slope-orientation reasoning; hillshade relief easily reads inverted, so a judge can flag correct images (I initially misjudged krea and qwen_nope).
examples: phi72/krea2_turbo: NW wall in shadow, SE wall lit = correct for NW light
issues.proposed_fix: Require the judge to name a specific slope and its facing direction as evidence; if the relief could be read inverted, mark 'unverifiable' instead of present.

issues.problem: Prompt-requested signage in photos ('warning placards', 'labeled floor') is intended text but is small and photographic; the design-role test in v2 does not settle it.
issues.proposed_fix: Text explicitly requested by the prompt is A02 regardless of size; unrequested incidental text is A03.

issues.problem: Only real trademarks/persons/landmarks; fictional copyrighted characters are not covered.
issues.proposed_fix: Extend C01 to 'recognisable copyrighted fictional characters'.

issues.problem: Objects implied by world knowledge but not requested (pieces on a chessboard) — unclear if extras.
examples: orig432: flux3_klein, gpt_image_2*, sunburst* add full chess sets
issues.proposed_fix: Implied accessories are fine unless they become the focal content or hide a requested attribute; then minor-moderate B07.

issues.problem: When a prompt asks for one uniform medium (e.g. 'entire artwork pointillist') and the model applies it to the background only, both A15 (style leak) and B05 fire for the same pixels. The rubric doesn't say whether to double-record or which one sets severity.
examples: orig323/fibo2_dev: realistic-fur panda over a dotted sky
orig323/qwen_image_2p1_pe: near-photo grass under a painted sky
issues.proposed_fix: Record A15 when elements differ in medium from each other. Record B05 when the whole image misses the requested medium (orig323/gemini, ideogram). If both apply, put the severity on A15 and mark B05 'partial'.

issues.criterion: A02 vs A03 for requested-but-unspecified text
issues.problem: The prompt asks for 'cardboard signs and banners' but gives no wording. Is gibberish sign text A02 (part of the design) or A03 (incidental)? The signs are focal in a protest scene.
issues.proposed_fix: Requested text carriers whose wording is unspecified go to A03, at moderate severity when they sit in the focal area. A02 stays for text whose wording is specified, or for text that is the subject.

issues.problem: A09 could fire on an object caught mid-fall (krea apple). In a photo that is a legitimate frozen-motion moment.
issues.proposed_fix: Add an exclusion: objects plausibly in motion (falling, thrown, splashing droplets) are not A09. Check only whether the motion is consistent.

issues.problem: Strong models fill scenes with real-world names (YMCA, Universal Robots, Dell, Mitutoyo, Hawaiki, SF Muni routes, Portland street signs). C01 gives no severity guidance or threshold.
issues.proposed_fix: Split C01 into C01a, a logo or brand mark on the focal object, and C01b, an incidental real name or street sign. Report C01b only, with no severity.

issues.problem: It is unclear whether the unit must appear on every label or only in the legend.
issues.proposed_fix: The unit is satisfied if a legend or axis title states it. Flag only when no unit appears anywhere.

issues.problem: 'A frame hanging in the center' could mean the centre of the wall or the centre of the image. Most models put the frame right of the image centre to make room for the vases.
issues.proposed_fix: Read placement words relative to the named reference object (here the wall). Do not flag when the reference extends beyond the frame.

issues.problem: Explicit exclusions of a body part ('with no tail') are routinely violated (7/12 models) and it is unclear whether to log B02, B03 or B07.
examples: orig96/gemini, ideogram, krea, qwen x2, fibo: tail present
issues.proposed_fix: State in B07 (or new B09 negation) that any explicitly excluded object, part or attribute that is present is major when on the focal subject.

issues.problem: Standard-design objects (traffic signs) rendered with wrong canonical shape while text is correct; or hybrid of two sign designs.
examples: phi452: 5 models draw a yellow diamond YIELD; sunburst draws red yield triangle inside diamond
issues.proposed_fix: Add: regulatory signs, flags, instruments must have the canonical shape for the stated type; a merged design of two standards is A10.

issues.problem: Dashcam OSD timestamp/speed bar is a requested-by-implication overlay ('dashcam view'), and could be over-flagged as subtitle bar.
issues.proposed_fix: Overlays native to a requested capture device (dashcam OSD, CCTV timestamp, viewfinder HUD) are not A16.

issues.problem: Does not mention instrument contents vs produced marks, or self-luminous-looking passive objects under flat light.
examples: orig574/qwen_image_2p1_nope brown lines from white cream
phi452/qwen_image_2p1_nope sign glowing like a lightbox under overcast
issues.proposed_fix: Add examples: 'white icing bag makes white lines', 'non-emissive sign does not glow under overcast'.

issues.problem: Prompts asking for two people with matching outfits produce identical faces; v2 gives no severity or A06 vs A13 rule.
issues.proposed_fix: State: identical face on 2+ people is A06 (moderate; major when they are the focal pair and also share pose), regardless of matching costume; A13 only for crowds of 3+.

issues.problem: Sign names in caps without quotes ('DO NOT ENTER sign') – unclear whether wording is required; half the models render a wordless roundel.
issues.proposed_fix: Treat unquoted sign names as type descriptors: missing wording is at most minor B04; quoted strings are required.

issues.problem: 'translucent hologram' is almost always rendered as an opaque planet; judges need an explicit check.
issues.proposed_fix: Add translucency/holographic/glass looks to the B05 looks list: opaque rendering of a requested translucent element is a miss.

issues.problem: Dashcam timestamp OSD and similar genre UI is requested-genre content, not a watermark; but small generator sparkle logos in corners are real A16.
issues.proposed_fix: A16 exception: overlays native to the requested capture genre (dashcam OSD, CCTV stamp, camera viewfinder) are not defects; explicitly list 'generator logo glyph in a corner' as A16.

issues.problem: Industrial prompts asking for 'wide shot showing rails, cable carriers' get close-ups; B08 examples focus on people.
issues.proposed_fix: Add example: requested wide/establishing shot rendered as a detail close-up, or a landmark whose full silhouette is requested cut by the frame, is major B08.

issues.problem: The prompt asks for unquoted text ('elegant printed text' on book pages). Neither A02 (intended) nor A03 (incidental) clearly applies, and severity differs.
examples: orig230/flux3_klein, qwen_image_2p1_nope: full pages of pseudo-text
issues.proposed_fix: Requested but unspecified text: judge legibility under A03 with severity one step higher (moderate when it covers a focal surface). There is no B04 because there is no target string.

issues.problem: Prompts with negations ('thornless', 'no sharp accessories') are often violated (spines). v2 gives no severity anchor, so judges treat spines as natural cactus detail.
issues.proposed_fix: Add to B05/B07: an explicitly negated attribute that is present on the focal subject is at least moderate, and major when it is prominent across the subject.

issues.problem: 'looking up at', 'gazing at' are judged from the head pose. The pupils often point elsewhere.
examples: orig355/qwen_image_2p1_nope: giant's pupils look away from the hamster
orig355/flux3_klein: both characters look at the camera
issues.proposed_fix: For a requested gaze, trace the pupil and head direction to the target. Looking at the camera counts as a miss.

issues.problem: Prompt adjectives turned into in-scene signage are missed because B04 reads like a caption rule.
issues.proposed_fix: State that B04 leakage includes signs, billboards and labels that restate prompt words or the quoted string somewhere other than the requested location.

issues.problem: Photoreal industrial prompts get real OEM branding on almost every gpt/gemini image (FANUC, KUKA, ARBURG, NISSEI, COBOD, EMOTIV), sometimes with the wrong model number ('HITACHI SE180DU').
issues.proposed_fix: Keep C01 as a flag but add a sub-flag 'brand_model_mismatch'. A wrong pairing is a factual error that could go to Layer A (A19) as well.

issues.problem: Small AI-provenance sparkle marks look like glints and are not listed.
issues.proposed_fix: Name 'generator provenance marks (sparkle/star logos in a corner)' under A16, always at least moderate.

traps.description: Requested on-screen overlays (CCTV timestamp, camera ID) look like A16 subtitle bars but are required; only judge them under A02/B04.
Recognizable real artworks/landmarks in a historically-themed prompt (Mona Lisa, Vitruvian Man, Big Ben) are C01 flags, not Layer A defects.
Motion blur on foreground balls could be read as A21, but here it is a B05 miss (prompt asked frozen crisp motion); do not double-count under A21.
Earth shown much larger/closer than physically possible next to Saturn/Jupiter is surreal intent (prompt says surrealism); not A20.
Avatar elements (bandana, ears) breaking a circular mask can be a deliberate 'pop-out' design, flag only minor at most.
Vertical wrecking-ball cable during 'mid-swing' is physically correct (bottom of arc); do not flag as not swinging.
Tape over patient eyes, face shields, eye protection during intubation are real clinical practice, not anomalies.
Motion blur on a LiDAR head expresses 'spinning' and is requested, not A21.
Upside-down face (camera at patient's feet looking at the chin) reads as melted/odd anatomy at a glance but is correct foreshortening.
Gown displayed on headless dress form - reads as missing head but is a mannequin; only a B question.
Blurred potted plant outside the window looks like a ghost/duplicate reflection but is just a balcony object behind glass.
Seals, signatures and inscriptions in a requested traditional Chinese painting are medium conventions, not A16 overlays; well-formed ones are not defects.
Dali-style long-legged elephants and figures in a prompt requesting 'Dali-esque' are requested style, not B07 extras.
Fisheye bezel, REC dot and dark vignette in a prompt that asks for a surveillance camera view are requested look, not A16 border/vignette.
Mirrored text reflected on an adjacent glossy ball is correct physics, not A03 mirrored pseudo-text.
examples: phi507/gemini_3_1_flash_image: red ball shows mirrored reflection of 'SALUC' printing

traps.description: Ghost/streak of a ball in requested motion blur, and pink reflection disc of the red ball on the cue ball, are not A07 duplicates.
Android robot elbows on table with hands clasped can look like 4 arms at preview size; trace each forearm before calling A05.
Dashcam overlays (timestamp, speed) and dashcam fisheye vignettes are genre-appropriate when a dashcam view is requested; they should not be A16, unless they write prompt words or cover content.
Regional variants of road signs (UK "GIVE WAY", Nordic red-yellow yield sign, triangle give-way road marking) are correct realisations of a "triangular yield sign", not B02 or A19.
Requested brand text on the requested product (Boston Dynamics on Spot) is correct Layer B content; flag C01 only as a risk, not as a defect.
Unrequested background planets, moons and galaxies in a space scene, and unrequested robot model labels (AURA, HOME-BOT), serve the scene and are not B07.
Herds of similar animals are naturally similar; A13 should fire only for identical pose or markings, or rigid even spacing, not for the same species and colour.
examples: orig276/gpt_image_2 varied herd = fine vs orig276/flux3_klein_base clones

traps.description: Glowing exterior of a crucible just out of a furnace is physically correct, not a lighting error.

Unrequested logo title text ('READING COACH', 'GUIDING THE WAY TO SUCCESS') on a logo prompt serves the design; flag only if it displaces requested text (B04 'prompt words written as unrequested text' may over-flag).
Second blurred Notre Dame / Eiffel tower in the bokeh background of a Paris app is scene-appropriate, not A07.
Motion blur of road foreground in a moving dashcam shot is motivated, not A21.
Rear-view mirror at the top of a dashcam frame is plausible camera placement.
Blank UI buttons are acceptable when the prompt only says 'function buttons'; don't flag A02/B04.
Prompt self-contradiction: 'slight camera shake suggests vibration' plus '1/1000s to freeze the spray'. A sharp image should not be penalised for missing shake under B05.
examples: phi533: all 12 images are sharp; none should get B05 for 'no camera shake'

traps.description: Correct mirror reflections of text on a glossy car hood (reversed letters) are physics, not A03 pseudo-text.
examples: phi414/ideogram4_nf4: 'CITY SANITATION' reflected reversed on the hood

traps.description: Cartoon hedgehog 'curled into a ball' with a face peeking out is a style convention; don't flag B03 unless the hedgehog is clearly uncurled (walking or lying in profile).
examples: orig53/gpt_image_2*: round spiky ball with face — fine

traps.description: Rainbow caustics spread widely over a dark floor around a crystal sculpture under spotlights are plausible dispersion, not A23 over-processing, unless they appear where no light passes through the crystal.
Licence plates, council names and street signs that are readable real-format text (e.g. 'BX70 KZV', 'Southwark Council') are not A03 defects; they may deserve C01 at most.
Robot push-ups on closed fists ('knuckle push-ups') match 'knuckle-like joints' and are not hand anatomy errors.
Overlays that the prompt's genre implies (dashcam OSD, aged photo border, film scratches/dust) are not A16 or A22.
Floating 3D road shields or labels in a "Google Earth style" render follow the requested UI style; they are not pseudo-text or overlays.
A requested real landmark (Statue of Liberty, Giza pyramids, Manhattan skyline) should not be counted as a C01 risk the same way as an unrequested brand.
Extra but scene-serving elements (camel rider in pyramids, glass UI cards in a glassmorphism image, distant camels) should not be B07.
Hand placement offset from imprint (hand lifted away after pressing) is correct for "just releases pressure"; do not flag missing contact.
Motion-blurred or ghosted wiper blades are requested (mid-swipe) and are not A07 duplicates.
Dashcam/camera OSD (timestamp, REC dot) when the prompt asks for a dashcam view is genre-appropriate, not A16.
Requested text degradation (rain-blurred letters) should not be read as A02 misspelling.
Animal paw with palm/pads facing the viewer and claws curled toward the viewer around a leaf is a consistent grip, not the A04 'palm faces camera while fingers curl over front' error.
Hillshade light-direction judgements: a correctly lit DEM can look wrong when relief is perceived inverted; verify a named slope before flagging.
Floating bookshelves, floating islands and books in a fantasy 'suspended library' are style intent, not A09.

Dashcam on-screen timestamp and fisheye or dark lens vignette when the prompt asks for a dashcam view. Under A16 these could be flagged as a 'subtitle bar' or 'vignette frame', but they belong to the requested capture device.
Unrequested on-theme props and signage (a Principia book next to Newton, safety signs in a scrapyard, lab signs). B07 should not fire; they serve the scene.
Requested haze or glare that softens the image is not A21/A23.
examples: phi80/flux3_klein_base: diagonal glare streak on the monitor

traps.description: Asymmetric but buildable designs (different-coloured pontoons, robots with no head) are not A10.
examples: phi208/flux3_klein: one white and one orange pontoon
orig200/flux3_klein: headless robot with a claw arm

traps.description: Text written by a subject facing the camera appears upside-down/mirrored to the viewer; this is physically correct and should be transcribed after rotating, not flagged.
examples: orig574/gemini_3_1_flash_image cake text reads from chef's side

traps.description: Reflections of text on glossy surfaces are correctly mirrored and should not count as A03 mirrored characters.
examples: phi452/gemini_3_1_flash_image hood reflection of YIELD sign reads mirrored

traps.description: Dashcam timestamp/speed overlay when a dashcam view is requested is genre-appropriate, not A16.
Robot covered in a protective paint suit looks like a draped cloth blob but is realistic paint-booth practice.
Prompt-requested colour that contradicts modern convention (yellow YIELD sign = pre-1971 US) should not be flagged; only the shape error counts.
Dashcam hood/windshield edge occupying the bottom of frame and timestamp OSD are requested by 'dashcam image' – not A16/A17 occlusion.
Laika statue wearing a harness/vest is historically accurate, not an unrequested extra.
Paris storefront signs ('CAFE FLORE', 'LIBRAIRIE', 'PONT D'IENA') in Ghibli scenes are correct incidental text and scene-serving extras; don't flag as B07.
Inkjet/dispensing heads with visible thin fluid stream are plausible; only flag when the stream does not reach the work or falls from far above.
Correct non-Latin text in cyberpunk scenes is easy to over-flag as pseudo-text. Read the script before calling A03.
examples: orig479/gpt_image_2: '未来は死んだ' is correct Japanese
orig479/qwen_image_2p1_pe: '未来已死', '機械' are correct

traps.description: Requested reflections can look like ghost duplicates.
examples: phi353/qwen_image_2p1_nope: faint reflection of the head cap on the safety glass (requested 'subtle reflections')
phi477/gpt_image_2_quality_high: reflection of the sign on the car hood

traps.description: Prompt-mandated impossibilities are not A12: lava poured onto a flower that does not burn, a hologram floating beside the chest.
examples: orig593/flux3_klein_base: screen floating off the chest

traps.description: Insect leg counts on thin or partly occluded legs are unreliable at 1024px. Flag B01 only when the count is clearly not 6.
examples: orig230: most butterflies show 4-6 visible legs with others hidden behind wings

traps.description: Stylised character limbs (a cactus arm ending in a rounded fold, a cactus with stubby legs) are style choices in non-photographic mode, not A04/A05 defects.
